items.stem: Name the systems in animals which help in the process of control and coordination.
items.answer: (i) Nervous system. (ii) Hormonal (endocrine) system.

items.stem: Write the functional and structural unit of the nervous system.
items.answer: Nerve cell or neuron.

items.stem: Which is the largest cell in the human body?
items.answer: Nerve cell or neuron.

items.stem: What are the main divisions of nervous system?
items.answer: The nervous system is broadly divisible into two parts: (i) Central nervous system, (ii) Peripheral nervous system.

items.stem: What do you mean by neuron?
items.answer: A neuron or nerve cell is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

items.stem: What are the various parts of the nervous system?
items.answer: The various parts of the nervous system are the brain, the spinal cord and the nerves.

items.stem: What do you understand by response to stimulus?
items.answer: Any change in the environment stimulates an organism to respond. This is known as response to stimulus.

items.stem: How do amoeba behave in warm water?
items.answer: In warm water, amoeba tend to aggregate together.

items.stem: Why do amoeba tend to aggregate together in warm water?
items.answer: Amoeba tend to aggregate together in warm water in response to the stimulus of temperature.

items.stem: Apart from nervous system, there is another system which controls and coordinates various functions of the body. Name it.
items.answer: It is the endocrine or hormonal system which also controls and coordinates various functions of the body.

items.stem: A car driver suddenly applies brakes after finding that a child is crossing the road in front of his speeding car. Which organ system was the first to become operative in this act?
items.answer: Nervous system.

items.stem: What is the action done suddenly called?
items.answer: Reflex action.

items.stem: Reflex actions are performed by a specific part of the nervous system. Name it.
items.answer: Spinal cord.

items.stem: What is the path of reflex actions called?
items.answer: Reflex arc.

items.stem: Name the main controlling part of the nervous system.
items.answer: Brain.

items.stem: Which of the following statements are true? (i) Sudden action in response to something in the environment is called reflex action. (ii) Sensory neurons carry signals from spinal cord to muscles. (iii) Motor neurons carry signals from receptors to spinal cord. (iv) The path through which signals are transmitted from a receptor to a muscle or a gland is called reflex arc.
items.answer: (c) (i) and (iv)

items.stem: Which of the following statements are true about the brain? (i) The main thinking part of brain is hind brain. (ii) Centres of hearing, smell, memory, sight etc. are located in fore brain. (iii) Involuntary actions like salivation, vomiting, blood pressure are controlled by the medulla in the hind brain. (iv) Cerebellum does not control posture and balance of the body.
items.answer: (c) (ii) and (iii)

items.stem: Posture and balance of the body is controlled by
items.answer: (b) cerebellum

items.stem: Spinal cord originates from
items.answer: (b) medulla

items.answer: (c) inhibit growth

items.stem: Which of the following is not associated with growth of plant?
items.answer: (d) Abscisic acid

items.stem: Name the substances which are involved in the control and coordination between environment and plant responses.
items.answer: Phytohormones and phytochromes are involved in the control and coordination between environment and plant responses.

items.stem: In plants, nastic movement and breaking of dormancy are controlled by which of the following - phytohormone or phytochrome?
items.answer: Nastic movement and breaking of dormancy are controlled by phytohormone.

items.stem: State the main function of abscisic acid in plants.
items.answer: It inhibits germination of seeds.

items.stem: Name the plant hormone responsible for the promotion of cell division.
items.answer: Cytokinin.

items.stem: What do we call the movement of shoot towards light?
items.answer: Phototropism.

items.answer: Auxin.

items.stem: Name the substances which are responsible for chemical coordination in animals.
items.answer: Hormones.

items.stem: Name the chemicals which transmit the informations in animals.
items.answer: Hormones.

items.stem: Name the glands which secrete these chemicals.
items.answer: Endocrine glands.

items.stem: Name the scientists who gave the term hormone.
items.answer: The term hormone was given by Bayliss and Starling.

items.stem: The coordination and control of all the hormone-producing glands is lost in a person. Which gland in such an individual may have become non-functional?
items.answer: Pituitary gland.

items.stem: Name the hormone which acts opposite to glucagon.
items.answer: Insulin.

items.stem: Name the endocrine glands which produce gametes.
items.answer: The testes and ovary produce gametes.

items.stem: If you find a large swelling in the neck projecting outward, which category of secretions you think is being produced in shortage?
items.answer: Thyroxin hormone. Its shortage causes simple goitre.

items.stem: Name the hormone secreted by parathyroid glands and give its one function.
items.answer: Parathyroid secretes calcitonin or parathormone which regulates blood calcium and phosphate.

items.stem: Which hormone helps in lowering the level of blood glucose in human beings?
items.answer: Insulin helps in lowering the level of blood glucose in human beings.

items.stem: Name the disease caused due to failure of insulin secretion.
items.answer: Diabetes mellitus is caused due to failure of insulin secretion.

items.stem: What is tropism? Describe the types of tropism. Mention two differences between tropism and nastic movement.
items.answer:
Tropism : It is a change in the direction of a part of a plant in response to other stimuli. Types of tropism : Geotropism, phototropism, hydrotropism, chemotropism, etc.
TropismNastic movement
(i)It is slow response towards any stimulus.It is an immediate response towards a stimulus.
(ii)It is directional.It is non-directional.

items.stem: Why are endocrine glands also called ductless glands?
items.answer: Endocrine glands are also called ductless glands because they do not have ducts, rather they pour their secretions directly into the blood. The blood takes these hormones to their target organs.
items.ocr: Section heading not printed in the extracted text; inferred from the numbering band (see item 167).

items.stem: List the characteristics of hormones.
items.answer: Hormones have the following characteristics: (i) They are secreted by an endocrine gland. (ii) They are specific chemical regulators. (iii) They are poured directly into the blood and are circulated through it. (iv) They act on a specific tissue or organ called target organ. (v) Their excess or deficiency may lead to serious consequences.
items.ocr: Section heading not printed in the extracted text; inferred from the numbering band (see item 167).

items.answer: (i) Hypothalamus (ii) Pituitary (iii) Pineal (iv) Thyroid (v) Parathyroid (vi) Pancreas (vii) Adrenal (viii) Testis (ix) Ovary

items.stem: Why is pituitary gland also called the master gland?
items.answer: The pituitary gland is called the master gland because it controls and coordinates the secretion of all the other endocrine glands.
items.ocr: Section heading not printed in the extracted text; inferred from the numbering band (see item 167).

items.stem: State the main function of pituitary gland. Write the effect of (i) excessive and (ii) sluggish activity of this gland on the growth of a child.
items.answer: The main function of pituitary gland is to control the other endocrine glands and the development of bones and muscles. Excessive activity of this gland leads to gigantism and sluggish activity of this gland leads to dwarfism.
items.ocr: Section heading not printed in the extracted text; inferred from the numbering band (see item 167).

items.stem: How does feedback mechanism regulate the hormone secretion? Or, cite an example to explain feedback mechanism for regulation of hormonal secretion.
items.answer: The feedback mechanism regulates the timing and amount of hormone to be secreted, e.g., if a person has more sugar in his blood this is detected by the cells of the pancreas. As a result, more insulin will be secreted to oxidise the sugar. In a reverse situation, the secretion of insulin will be depleted.
